newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Russia-Greece oil route linked to Caspian pipeline.
newsitem.headline: Russia-Greece oil route linked to Caspian pipeline.

text.p: A planned oil route from Russia to Greece via Bulgaria will be part of a greater regional project linking the Black Sea to a Caspian Sea oil pipeline, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister said on Wednesday.
"The new development is that we are no longer looking at the Balkan oil pipeline project as a Russia-Bulgaria-Greece oil route only but in a wider context," Doncho Konakchiev said.
"(We look at it) as a project of the whole region: the Caspian Sea and the Black Sea as a united system for extraction, transportation and realisation of the crude oil," he told reporters.

Russia, Bulgaria and Greece plan a tanker route from Russia's Novorossiisk to Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Bourgas from where a new high-pressure pipeline would carry Russian crude oil to Alexandroupolis in Greece.
Bulgaria's biggest refinery, Neftohim in Bourgas, will refine part of the crude, Konakchiev said.

A tripartite meeting at government level is expected soon, he said, adding that the meeting had been delayed due to the elections in Russia and Greece. Bulgaria also has a presidential election on October 27.
"Following the talks we had with the Russian and the Greek sides I think that the spirit is categorically in favour of the project's realisation," Konakchiev said.
He said he had discussed with Mobil Oil Corp's deputy president how the firm could provide know-how from its experience with similar projects in the former Soviet Union.
"If our partners from Russia and Greece agree, we will have them as consultants," Konakchiev said.
He said he had also met officials from Chevron Corp and Russia's Rosneft and Lukoil. He gave no further details.

Mobil, Chevron, Rosneft and Lukoil are part of the Caspian Pipeline Consortium Ltd, whose project is to send oil through an as yet unbuilt pipeline around the Caspian Sea across Russia and to its Novorossiisk port at the Black Sea.
The 1,500-km (940-mile) pipeline may carry oil not only from the Kazakh's Tengiz oil field but also from an Azeri-led Caspian Sea project as well as Russian oil.
